newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls Iraq dialogue offer "comical".
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls Iraq dialogue offer "comical".

text.p: The United States on Thursday dismissed as an "almost comical offer" a suggestion by an official Iraqi newspaper that Baghdad was prepared to open a dialogue with Washington.

Al-Thawra, mouthpiece of the ruling Baath Party, said Iraq realised that the United States had vital interests in the Gulf. "Iraq has no interest in fighting the United States or being hostile to it. It has more than one advantage in dealing with it," it said.
"This is really an almost comical offer," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

Burns said that if Iraqi President Saddam Hussein wanted a dialogue he first had to fulfil U.N. resolutions stemming from Iraq's 1991 Gulf War defeat, "and he hasn't done that in any way, shape or form."
"So there's no reason for us to have a dialogue with him when he continues to try to cheat on the U.N. sanctions," Burns told reporters.
"There's a lot he needs to answer for. He can't get away with this cheap offer and expect that we're going to take it seriously."

U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990 are still in force. Washington says that for them to be lifted Iraq must prove it has done away with its weapons of mass destruction, account for missing Kuwaitis and meet other demands.
